questions.question: The salary of a typist was at first raised by 20% and then it was reduced by 5%. He presently draws Rs.17,100. What was his original salary (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The salary of typist increased = 20%

The change in salary of the typist is decreased = 5%

After Increment of 20% & decrement of 5% his present salary = 17100

**Calculation:**

Let the original salary be 'x'

After 20% of increment of salary of typist = x + 20% of x

⇒ x(1 + 20%) = x(1 + 20/100)

⇒ x(100 + 20)/100 = 120x/100

⇒ 120x/100 = 6x/5

After decremnt of 5% salalry of typist = 6x/5 - 5% of 6x/5

⇒ (6x/5)(1 - 5%) = (6x/5)(1 - 5/100)

⇒ (6x/5)(100 - 5)/100 = (6x/5)(95/100)

⇒ 57/50x

Salary of typist after increment and decrement = 57x/50

57x/50 = 17100

⇒ x = 17100 × 50/51

⇒ x = 15000

**∴ The salary of typist initially is Rs. 15000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

x × (120/100) × (95/100) = 17100

⇒ x = 17100 × (100/120) × (100/95)

⇒ x = 15000

questions.question:
A 5-m-deep cylindrical pit having a radius of 1.4 m is dug in a field. The earth so dug out is used to raise a platform of 10 m × 8 m. What is the height of the platform (in cm)?

( {{Use} pi = frac{{22}}{7}} )
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of a cylinder = 1.4 m 

Height of a cylinder = 5 m

The earth raise platform = 10 × 8 × h

**Concept Used:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h where r is the radius of the base

And h is the height of the cylinder

Volume of cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

**Calculations:**

Volume of a cylinder = volume of cuboid 

⇒ (22/7) × 1.4 × 1.4 × 5 = 10 × 8 × h

⇒ (22/7) × 1.4 × 0.7 = 8 × h

⇒ h = (22/7) × 1.4 × 0.7/8

⇒ h = 0.385 m

⇒ h = 38.5 cm

**∴ The height of the platform is 38.5 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: An article is sold for Rs.796.875, after allowing two successive discounts of 15% and 25%. The cost price of the article is Rs.1,000. If it is sold at the marked price, then what is the gain percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The selling price of an article = Rs. 796.875

Two successive discounts = 15% and 25% respectively

The cost price of the article = Rs.1,000

**Formula used:**

Gain = selling price - cost price

Gain% = (gain/cost price) × 100

**Calculations:**

Let the marked price be x

After allowing First discount 15% = x - 15%x

⇒ x(1 - 15/100) = x(100 - 15)/100

⇒ x × 85/100 = 17x/20

After allowing Second discount 25% = 17x/20 - (17x/20) 25%

⇒(17x/20)(1 - 25/100) = (17x/20)(100 - 25)/100

questions.question: 10 men can finish a piece of work in 10 days, whereas it takes 12 women to finish it in 10 days. If 8 men and 6 women undertake to complete the work, then in how many days will they complete it?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio: 10 **Men** × 10 = 12 **Women** × 10 ⇒ 5 **Men** = 6 **Women**.

Total Work = 10 **Men** × 10 days = 100 **Man-days**.

Group Efficiency = 8 **Men** + 6 **Women** = 8 **Men** + 5 **Men** = 13 **Men**.

Required Days = 100 ÷ 13 = 7 9/13 **days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 9/13 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 10 **Men** (M) in 10 days; 12 **Women** (W) in 10 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = M × D × E (Efficiency); Days = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 10 **Men** 10 600 60 
 12 **Women** 10 60 

⇒ Efficiency of 1 **Man** = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 1 **Woman** = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units/day

⇒ Total Work = 10 × 10 × 6 = 600 units

⇒ Efficiency of (8 **Men** + 6 **Women**) = (8 × 6) + (6 × 5) = 48 + 30 = 78 units/day

⇒ Required Days = 600 ÷ 78 = 100 ÷ 13 = 7 9/13 days

**∴ The correct answer is 7 9/13 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

**M₁D₁H₁ Formula**

The relation between **men**, **days**, and **work** is (M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂.

**Efficiency and Time**

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to the **time** taken to complete the work (E ∝ 1/T).

**Combined Work**

When multiple groups work together, their **individual efficiencies** are added to find the **total rate** of work.</p

questions.question: A person invested one-third of his money at 3(1)/(2)\% , one-fourth of his money at 7(1)/(2)\% , and the remaining at 8% per annum simple interest. If his yearly simple interest is Rs.1,479, then what is the sum invested (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person invested one-third of his money at the rate of interest = 3(1)/(2)\% 

One-fourth of his money at the rate of interest = 7(1)/(2)\% 

Remaining money at the rate of interest = 8%

Simple interest yearly = 1479

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = PTR/100

**Calculations:**

Let the sum of money be x

1/3rd of amount = x/3

1/4 th of amount = x/4

Reamining amount = x - x/3 - x/4

⇒ (12x - 4x - 3x)/12 = 5x/12

Simple interst = [(x/3) × 3(1)/(2) + (x/4)( 7(1)/(2)) + (5x/12) × 8]/100

⇒ [(x/3) × (7/2) + (x/4)(15/2) + (5x/12) × 8]/100 = [(7x/6 + 15x/8 + 40x/2]/100

⇒ [(28x + 45x + 80x)/24]/100 = 153x/2400

Accordingly,

1479 = 153x/2400

⇒ x = 1479 × 2400/153

⇒ x = 23200

**∴ The sum of amount is 23200**

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys 50 kg of sugar from a dealer, keeps 5 kg for his own use, and tries to sell the rest at a certain fixed price. He sells 15 kg at that fixed price. Then, he offers a discount of 10% and sells 10 kg at this discounted price. Finally, he offers an additional 25% discount over the discounted price and manages to sell all the sugar he had left with him. He gets a total of Rs.1,875 after selling the sugar and makes an overall profit of 20%. If he could have sold the entire 50 kg sugar at its original fixed price without any discount, then what would have been his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Revenue Units (in terms of fixed price P) = (15 × 1) + (10 × 0.9) + (20 × 0.9 × 0.75) = 15 + 9 + 13.5 = 37.5 units.

Total Revenue ₹1875 ⇒ Fixed price per kg (P) = 1875 ÷ 37.5 = ₹50.

Total Cost Price (CP) of 50 kg = Total Revenue ÷ 120% = 1875 ÷ 1.2 = ₹1562.5.

Revenue if all 50 kg sold at fixed price = 50 × 50 = ₹2500.

Profit % = (2500 − 1562.5) ÷ 1562.5 × 100 = 937.5 ÷ 1562.5 × 100 = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sugar = 50 kg | Kept for use = 5 kg | Sugar for sale = 45 kg

Total SP = ₹1875 | Profit = 20%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (1 + Profit/100) | Discounted Price = Marked Price × (1 − Discount/100)

 
 
• 
 
• 
 15 kg @ P
 10 kg @ 0.9P
 20 kg @ 0.675P
 

 Total Revenue = ₹1,875
 
 Total CP = ₹1,562.5
 
 Fixed Price P = ₹50/kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP of 50 kg sugar = 1875 ÷ 1.2 = ₹1562.5

⇒ Let Fixed Price be P. Total kg for sale = 50 − 5 = 45 kg

⇒ SP₁ (15 kg) = 15 × P

⇒ SP₂ (10 kg) = 10 × (0.9P) = 9P

⇒ SP₃ (Remaining 20 kg) = 20 × (0.9P × 0.75) = 20 × 0.675P = 13.5P

⇒ Total SP = 15P + 9P + 13.5P = 37.5P

⇒ 37.5P = 1875

⇒ P = 1875 ÷ 37.5 = ₹50 per kg

⇒ New SP for 50 kg = 50 × 50 = ₹2500

⇒ Profit = New SP − Total CP = 2500 − 1562.5 = ₹937.5

⇒ Profit % = (937.5 ÷ 1562.5) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 0.6 × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given on an article, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Profit and Loss on Variable Quantities

Profit % = [(Total Revenue − Total Cost) ÷ Total Cost] × 100. Always ensure the cost price is calculated for the same total quantity as the target selling quantity.

Marked Price Relationship

CP × (100 + Profit%) = MP × (100 − Discount%). This is used to find the ratio of CP to MP directly.

⇒ The area of the floor must be divisible by x²

questions.question: A car runs for 11 hours. For the first 100 km, the car runs with a certain speed and then it increases its speed by 15 km/h to cover the remaining 280 km. How much time (in hours) does it take to cover the first 100 km?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total time car runs = 11 hours

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance/speed

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the car initially be x

For the first 100 km car runs with speed = x km/hr

After 100 km car increases speed by 15 km/hr = x + 15

Remaining distance = 280 km 

Total time = 100/x + 280/(x + 15)

⇒ 11 = [(x + 15)100 + 280 × x]/[x(x + 15)]

⇒ 11 = (100x + 1500 + 280x )/(x² + 15x)

⇒ 11(x² + 15x) = 380x + 1500

⇒ 11x² + 165x = 380x + 1500

⇒ 11x2 + 165x - 380x - 1500 = 0

⇒ 11x2 - 215x - 1500 = 0

⇒ 11x² - 275x + 60x - 1500 = 0

⇒ 11x(x - 25) + 60(x - 25) = 0

⇒ (11x + 60)(x - 25) = 0

So, x = - 60/11 or x = 25

Speed can't be negative so, x = 25

Initially speed was 25 km/h

Required time to cover the first 100 km is 100/25 = 4 hours.

**∴ It takes 4 hours to cover the first 100 km.**
